text:

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Directly studies reward design for agents interacting with simulated users, comparing turn-level rewards and conversation-level scoring. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.09215v1)** — Builds adaptive user simulators with dynamic goals and strategic reasoning; uses multiple rewards to improve consistency and resistance to agent manipulation. **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, and colleagues. **Affiliations:** Meituan, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Dalian University of Technology.

3. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** — Introduces UserVille’s configurable user simulators and rewards combining task success, useful clarification, and alignment with user preferences. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University); Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).

4. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19336v1)** — Trains simulators using an LLM judge’s assessment of whether responses are indistinguishable from a particular human user’s responses. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Stanford University, and MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab.

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.09998v1)** (2026). Directly relevant to **within-run adaptation**: agents refine prompts, skills, memory, and subagents mid-episode; an extension jointly trains model weights. **People:** Seth Karten, Tersoo Upaa Jr., Ruirong Feng, Wenzhe Li, Chengshuai Shi, and Chi Jin — Princeton University; Joel Zhang — ARISE Foundation; Kiran Vodrahalli — Google DeepMind.

2. **[ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience](https://artificer-ai-lab.github.io/ASCENT/)**. Relevant to **adaptation across tasks**: verified execution experience produces persistent weight updates that improve subsequent attempts, contrasting with methods that reset adaptation after each episode. **People:** Haodong Lu and Dong Gong — Artificer AI Lab, University of New South Wales, Sydney.

3. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.11366v4)** (2023). Foundational work on **learning across trials through memory**: agents retain textual reflections from failures to improve later attempts without updating model weights. **People:** Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, and Edward Berman — Northeastern University; Ashwin Gopinath — MIT; Karthik Narasimhan and Shunyu Yao — Princeton University.

1. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19682v1)** — December 2025. A direct match: jointly trains an agent and a simulator that generates tasks suited to the agent’s changing abilities. **People:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton and ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao, Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed).

2. **[Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.18292v1)** — April 2026. Synthesizes executable tool environments and adapts tasks to capability gaps, enabling policies and environments to co-evolve. **People:** corresponding researchers Guanting Dong and Zhicheng Dou; team affiliations are **Renmin University of China and ByteDance Seed**.

3. **[Learning to Build the Environment: Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.14392v1)** — May 2026. Introduces **EvoEnv**, where one policy both constructs executable training environments and learns to solve their tasks. **People:** Yucheng Shi, Zhenwen Liang, Kishan Panaganti, Dian Yu, Wenhao Yu, Haitao Mi — **Tencent HY LLM**.

4. **[Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10299v1)** — August 2026. A useful survey covering agent–environment co-evolution through changing tasks, feedback, and interaction spaces. **People:** Qing Zong, Jiayu Liu, Junhao Shen, Zecong Tang, Linsi Wu, Yuxuan Liu, Rui Wang, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xiusi Chen, Yangqiu Song. **Affiliations represented:** HKUST, UIUC, Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Hong Kong, and Peking University.

5. **[Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.04128v1)** — September 2026. Closely related work that progressively increases environment difficulty and schedules successive generations during agent training. **People:** Zhiyuan Fan, Tinghao Yu, Yuanjun Cai, Jiang Zhou, Jiangtao Guan, Jincheng Liu, Yun Yang, Dingxin Hu, Zhuo Han, Xing Wu, Feng Zhang, Lilin Wang — **Hunyuan Team, Tencent**.

Relevant as an evaluation environment for interactive agents. **People:** Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra; Yao’s work was conducted during an internship).

text:

Qiu, and Yuqing Yang — **Microsoft Research**.

text:

Evolves diverse, human-like simulator personas; training on these interactions improves robustness to challenging user behavior. **People:** Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Chirag Shah, and Natasha Jaques (University of Washington); Tadayoshi Kohno (Georgetown University).
